title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a 'Rétrospection sur les cartes' (finite topological maps). On the previous page Grothendieck set up an equivalence between isotopy classes of cellular maps on compact (possibly non-orientable) surfaces and finite 'special' sets with an action of the cartographic group Γ2 = <τ0,τ1,τ∞ | τi²=1, (τ0τ∞)²=1>. 'Special' means that τ0, τ1, τ∞ and τ0τ∞ act without fixed points. He also introduced the index-2 even subgroup Γ2^0, generated by the ρ's.

Equation (5) fixes the generators:
- ρ∞ = τ1τ0,
- ρ1 = τ0τ∞,
- ρ0 = τ∞τ1.
Each ρ_i is the product of the two reflections other than τ_i. Hence ρ_i fixes the cell of type i: ρ0 rotates about the vertex, ρ1 about the edge midpoint, ρ∞ about the face centre. One checks ρ∞ρ1ρ0 = 1 and ρ1² = 1, as in relation (4).

The page then makes explicit the geometric meaning of a 'repère' (flag). A flag is a 2-simplex r of the barycentric subdivision. Its vertices are a vertex s = s̃ (type 0), the midpoint ã of an incident edge a (type 1), and the centre f̃ of an incident face f (type ∞). The reflection τ_i changes the type-i vertex of r.

A flag is equivalently a 'biarc': an edge a with two orientations.
- The tangential orientation leaves s ('origin' of a).
- The normal orientation enters f ('extremity face' of a).
- Mnemonic: 'one leaves the vertex to enter the face, passing through the edge a'.

The flag carries a local orientation of the surface, namely the cyclic order s → ã → f̃ of its vertices. Grothendieck checks two equivalent descriptions of it:
- the normal orientation of a gives the direct sense of rotation around s;
- the tangential orientation gives the direct sense of rotation around f.
The figure marks the direct rotation senses around all three vertices of r. The page breaks off while comparing, on closed paths around r, the orientations of the edge portions s̃ã, ãf̃, f̃s̃ with those of the portions turning around the vertices.

Purpose: this fixes sign and orientation conventions so that, on the next page, an orientation of the surface becomes a splitting R(X) = R+ ⊔ R- exchanged by the τ_i. Oriented maps then correspond to finite Γ2^0-sets (equivalently, via ρ1² = 1, to sets with a pair of permutations in which ρ1 is fixed-point-free). The same conventions control how duality (exchanging the types 0 and ∞) reverses the orientation of each flag.
errors: No mathematical errors. Relations (5) are consistent with (4): ρ∞ρ1ρ0 = τ1τ0·τ0τ∞·τ∞τ1 = 1 and ρ1² = (τ0τ∞)² = 1.

Orientation conventions are stated, not proved. The claimed equivalence of the three descriptions (cyclic order s ã f̃, normal orientation = direct rotation about s, tangential orientation = direct rotation about f) is a direct check on the figure.
The final sentence is incomplete (page cut off).

ideas.what: Cartographic group with generators ρ_i = products of pairs of the reflections τ_j, each rotating around the cell of type i.
ideas.modern_name: cartographic group C2 and its even (orientation-preserving) subgroup C2^+
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978) for the map/flag group formalism; Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) for the name 'cartographic group'; Malgoire–Voisin (1977) for the cartographic language in Montpellier

ideas.what: Flags (repères) identified with the triangles of the barycentric subdivision, with vertices of type 0, 1, ∞.
ideas.modern_name: flags of a map / barycentric subdivision (flag complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard combinatorial map theory (Tutte; Jones–Singerman; Lins)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (barycentric subdivision of a map, flags)

ideas.what: Biarc: a flag encoded as an edge with a tangential orientation (out of the vertex) and a normal orientation (into the face). The orientation of the flag triangle is related to the rotation senses around the vertex and the face.
ideas.modern_name: flag as edge with two orientations ('quarter-edge' / dart pair, as in the quad-edge structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Guibas–Stolfi quad-edge structure (1985) in computational geometry

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of orientation conventions for flags of a map in the barycentric subdivision. It is standard combinatorial map theory, already implicit in Jones–Singerman and in the Esquisse. The 'biarc' terminology is a minor personal touch with no new content.
transcription_corrections: 'Le biarc on donne' should read 'Le biarc (associé au repère r) donne comme orientation tangentielle celle qui sort du sommet s'. The word 'on' is a crossed-out fragment.
'par passant[?] par l'arête a' is likely 'en passant par l'arête a'.
'sens de rotation "directs" (pour l'orientation définie par r)' is correct. The insertion '(de l'arête a)' qualifies 'orientation normale'.

In the last lines, the inserted text above 'des arêtes' is the list s̃ã, ãf̃, f̃s̃. The phrase is roughly 'comparé à leur sens [with] les portions des parcours qui tournent autour des sommets'. The sentence is unfinished.
